tasks.title: Migration 042: server-owned history, server-write-only approvals, always-allow, page conversations, turn lock
tasks.interface: Idempotent, single transaction, header comment, 'smoke after apply' block. DDL: ALTER TABLE copilot_messages ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS parts jsonb, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS message_id text, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS seq integer; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS copilot_messages_conv_msg_uq ON copilot_messages(conversation_id, message_id) WHERE message_id IS NOT NULL. Existing copilot_messages policies are NOT changed (legacy client path must keep working until the code deploys). ALTER TABLE copilot_conversations ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS page_key text, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS turn_lock_until timestamptz; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS copilot_conversations_page_uq ON copilot_conversations(organization_id, user_id, page_key) WHERE page_key IS NOT NULL. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copilot_approvals (id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), organization_id uuid NOT NULL, user_id uuid NULL, conversation_id uuid NULL REFERENCES copilot_conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, task_id uuid NULL, tool_call_id text NOT NULL, approval_id text NULL, tool_name text NOT NULL, input jsonb NOT NULL, diff jsonb NOT NULL, source text NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('chat','task')), status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','denied','applied','failed','stale','expired')), result jsonb NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), resolved_at timestamptz NULL, UNIQUE (organization_id, tool_call_id)); CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS copilot_approvals_org_approval_uq ON copilot_approvals(organization_id, approval_id) WHERE approval_id IS NOT NULL; index (organization_id, status, created_at desc). ALTER TABLE ai_settings ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS copilot_always_allow jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb. ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on copilot_approvals with ONE policy: SELECT for org members using the 021 membership pattern; no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies (all writes go through the service role in lib/ai/approvals.ts). SYNTHESIS RULING: Turn lock: turn_lock_until is set to now() + 150 s (longer than the chat route's maxDuration of 120 s) together with a new column turn_lock_token uuid; release clears the lock only WHERE turn_lock_token = the caller's token, so a request whose lock expired can never clear a newer holder's lock. copilot_approvals stays server-write-only: members get SELECT only, with no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy. Existing copilot_messages policies are unchanged here; they are locked later by migration 044 (T30). The migration must also satisfy the repo-wide idempotency lint planned in verify-track (tests/migrations-idempotent.test.ts, which reads every 039-049 migration): a '--' header, exactly one BEGIN and one COMMIT, IF NOT EXISTS on every CREATE TABLE / ADD COLUMN / CREATE INDEX, DROP POLICY IF EXISTS before every CREATE POLICY, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, and every SECURITY DEFINER function sets search_path with REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC plus GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role; no DROP TABLE. TESTS MUST ASSERT (checked in review): asserts: applies 042 twice without error; UPDATE copilot_approvals SET status='approved' WHERE id=$1 AND status='pending' RETURNING id returns 1 row first and 0 rows second; status 'bogus' rejected; duplicate (organization_id, tool_call_id) rejected; two rows with approval_id NULL in the same org allowed; after setUser(memberUid) and SET ROLE authenticated an INSERT into copilot_approvals fails with an RLS error while a SELECT of that org's rows succeeds; legacy copilot_messages rows with NULL parts still select; the pre-042 INSERT policy on copilot_messages still allows a member insert PLAN FIX (orchestrator): copilot_approvals.organization_id REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (guest purge deletes orgs; task-sourced rows have no conversation to cascade from). Turn lock is acquired/released by the app with supabase-js, which cannot call now(): T9 computes expiry in the app (Date.now()+150000) and acquires with a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE turn_lock_until IS NULL OR turn_lock_until < <app now>.

tasks.title: Pure field-diff and staleness check
tasks.interface: export type FieldDiff = { kind: 'create' | 'update'; recordType: string; recordId?: string; fields: Array<{ name: string; before?: unknown; after: unknown }> }. export function computeFieldDiff(args: { toolName: string; input: Record<string, unknown>; current: Record<string, unknown> | null; recordType: string; idField?: string }): FieldDiff — current === null gives kind 'create' with every input key except the id field as {name, after}; otherwise kind 'update' listing only keys whose JSON-normalised value differs (dates normalised to YYYY-MM-DD, null and undefined equal, unchanged keys omitted). export function isDiffStale(diff: FieldDiff, live: Record<string, unknown> | null): boolean — true if kind 'update' and (live is null or any field.before no longer equals live[field.name]). Pure; no supabase imports. SYNTHESIS RULING: Diff fidelity: the diff is computed over the DB COLUMN PATCH the handler will actually write, not the raw tool input. computeFieldDiff therefore takes the patch produced by the tool's toPatch(input) (see T6), so mapped or defaulted fields appear on the card exactly as they will be written. FieldDiff also carries baselineUpdatedAt?: string (the record's updated_at when the diff was computed), which T6 uses as a write precondition. TESTS MUST ASSERT (checked in review): asserts: create diff lists all non-id fields; update diff omits unchanged; '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' equals '2026-10-01'; stale when live changed; stale when live null; not stale when only a non-diffed column changed

tasks.title: Shared tool registry and session/cron adapter over MCP definitions (copilot-origin automation allowlist, fan-out cap)
tasks.interface: policy.ts: export const COPILOT_READ_TOOLS: readonly string[] (the 12 MCP read tools by name); export const COPILOT_WRITE_TOOLS: readonly string[] (explicit allowlist: MCP write tools minus delete_record and minus any bulk tool); export const LOW_RISK_WRITES = ['save_artifact','save_memory','draft_email'] as const; export const NEVER_AUTO_ALLOW: readonly string[] (delete_record plus every bulk_* / *_many name in lib/mcp); export const WRITE_FANOUT_PER_TURN = 20; export const TASK_MODE_EXCLUDED = ['create_task'] as const; export function isAlwaysAllowed(toolName: string, alwaysAllow: unknown): boolean (false unless alwaysAllow is a string[] containing toolName AND toolName in COPILOT_WRITE_TOOLS AND not in NEVER_AUTO_ALLOW); export function sanitizeAlwaysAllow(input: unknown): string[]. labels.ts: export const TOOL_LABELS: Record<string, string> ('search_leads' -> 'Searched leads', 'draft_email' -> 'Drafted email', ...). registry.ts: export type CopilotToolEnv = { db: SupabaseClient; ctx: { orgId: string; userId: string | null; isGuest: boolean; source: 'chat' | 'task'; conversationId: string | null; taskId: string | null } } (no admin client field; callers pass the RLS client for sessions and an admin client with explicit orgId for cron); export type RegistryTool = { name; description; inputSchema: z.ZodObject; kind: 'read' | 'write' | 'low_risk_write'; recordType?: string; idField?: string; execute(input, env): Promise<unknown> }; export function listRegistryTools(mode: 'chat' | 'task'): RegistryTool[] (built from lib/mcp definitions by name through the allowlists plus the T7 copilot-only tools; task mode excludes TASK_MODE_EXCLUDED); export async function executeRegistryTool(name, input, env): Promise<{ ok: true; data: unknown } | { ok: false; error: string }> — validates input with zod, runs the MCP handler with {db: env.db, ctx: {orgId, scope: 'copilot', createdBy: env.ctx.userId}} and with automation firing disabled: the adapter passes whatever flag or injected dispatcher the handlers use (determine it by reading lib/mcp; if handlers import a dispatcher module directly, add an optional `automations?: 'off'` field to the MCP env type and gate the dispatch call on it — this is the one allowed MCP refactor); the result includes { automationsSkipped: true } for write tools. export function buildCopilotToolSet(env, opts: { alwaysAllow: string[]; onWriteRequested: (info: { toolCallId: string; toolName: string; input: unknown; diff: FieldDiff }) => Promise<void>; fanout?: { count: number } }): ToolSet — write tools get needsApproval: async (input, { toolCallId }) => { if (isAlwaysAllowed) return false; if (++fanout.count > WRITE_FANOUT_PER_TURN) throw a tool error 'fanout_limit: propose at most 20 changes per turn'; diff = computeFieldDiff(fetchCurrentRecord(env, recordType, idField, input)); await onWriteRequested({toolCallId, toolName, input, diff}); return true } and attach the diff as the approval descriptor if the SDK supports it; otherwise registry exports `pendingDescriptors: Map<toolCallId, FieldDiff>` which the route emits as a `data-approval-diff` part keyed by toolCallId (decide during this task by reading node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts and record the choice in a comment). Write execute(): re-fetch the live record, if isDiffStale return { ok:false, error:'record_changed' } else run executeRegistryTool. In env.ctx.source === 'task' mode write tools do not execute: they call onWriteRequested and return { queued: true }. Read tools never set needsApproval. Low-risk writes execute directly in both modes. SYNTHESIS RULING: (1) Each write tool exposes toPatch(input) => { table, id?, patch }, the exact column patch its handler writes. Refactor the handlers in lib/mcp/tools-write.ts so that toPatch is the single place that maps input to columns and the handler applies that patch. The MCP behaviour seen by outside clients (names, schemas, results) must stay identical; run the existing MCP tests (tests/mcp-server.test.ts). (2) Stale-write protection: when an approved update runs, executeRegistryTool applies the patch with an extra .eq('updated_at', diff.baselineUpdatedAt). If zero rows match, it returns { error: 'record_changed' } and writes nothing. That closes the race between the staleness check and the write. (3) Automations: Copilot-origin writes still fire automation rules, but evaluateLeadAgainstRules gains an options argument { origin?: 'copilot' }. For copilot origin, lib/automation/runner.ts runs only an ALLOWLIST of actions with no outbound effect (change_status, assign_to, update_field, add_activity, send_notification, add_tag); anything else, including enroll_sequence, which leads to emails being sent, and any action type added later, is skipped and recorded as { success: false, error: 'skipped_for_copilot' }. The write result carries automationsSkipped: string[] for the step trace. (4) Task mode: listRegistryTools('task') returns record-write tools with needsApproval false and an execute that ONLY records a pending approval (recordPendingApproval with source 'task') and returns { status: 'proposed', approvalRowId }. A scheduled run therefore always produces a durable proposal and never depends on SDK approval mid-run. Low-risk writes (save_artifact, save_memory, draft_email) execute normally in task mode. TESTS MUST ASSERT (checked in review): asserts: listRegistryTools('chat') never contains delete_record or any NEVER_AUTO_ALLOW name; listRegistryTools('task') contains no create_task; every write tool has needsApproval and every read tool lacks it; isAlwaysAllowed('delete_record', ['delete_record']) === false; with a recording fake SupabaseClient every exposed MCP handler applies .eq('organization_id', ctx.orgId) on each .from() chain or the test names the offender; the 21st write proposal in one toolset instance throws fanout_limit; the automation dispatcher is called with { origin: 'copilot' } for copilot lead writes; task mode returns queued without calling the handler; stale live record returns record_changed without calling the handler | asserts: with origin 'copilot' an enroll_sequence action is skipped and no sequence_enrollments insert happens, while add_tag runs; without origin, enroll_sequence runs as before PLAN FIX (orchestrator): in chat mode the fan-out limit must NOT throw (ai 6 aborts the whole stream): when the limit is reached, needsApproval returns false and execute returns { ok:false, error:'fanout_limit' } without writing. T6 may create lib/ai/tools/copilot-tools.ts as a stub exporting an empty copilotOnlyTools; T7 replaces it.

tasks.title: Approval store (service role, explicit org predicates) with early pending rows, atomic claim and staleness
tasks.interface: All functions take an admin SupabaseClient and every query carries .eq('organization_id', orgId). export type ApprovalResponse = { approvalId: string; approved: boolean; reason?: string }. export async function recordPendingApproval(admin, args: { orgId; userId: string | null; conversationId: string | null; taskId: string | null; source: 'chat'|'task'; toolCallId: string; toolName: string; input: unknown; diff: FieldDiff }): Promise<{ id: string }> (insert; on conflict (organization_id, tool_call_id) do nothing and return the existing id). export async function attachApprovalIds(admin, args: { orgId; conversationId; pairs: Array<{ toolCallId: string; approvalId: string }> }): Promise<void> (UPDATE ... SET approval_id WHERE organization_id AND conversation_id AND tool_call_id AND approval_id IS NULL). export async function claimApproval(admin, args: { orgId; conversationId: string | null; approvalId: string; approved: boolean }): Promise<{ status: 'claimed'; row } | { status: 'not_pending' } | { status: 'not_found' }> — single UPDATE SET status = approved ? 'approved' : 'denied', resolved_at = now() WHERE organization_id = $org AND approval_id = $id AND status = 'pending' AND conversation_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $conv RETURNING *; zero rows then a SELECT distinguishes not_found from not_pending. export async function markApprovalOutcome(admin, orgId, id, outcome: 'applied'|'failed'|'stale', result?: unknown). export async function listPendingApprovals(admin, orgId, opts?: { source?: 'chat'|'task' }). export async function expireApprovals(admin, olderThanHours = 72): Promise<number>. export function extractApprovalRequests(message: UIMessage): Array<{ toolCallId; approvalId; toolName }> (pure: parts in state 'approval-requested'). SYNTHESIS RULING: Approval rows store diff.baselineUpdatedAt. Since claimApproval UPDATEs pending to approved before execution: if execution then fails or returns record_changed, markApprovalOutcome sets the status to 'failed' or 'stale' (never back to 'pending'), so a retry is a fresh proposal. When a batch has several approval responses, each is claimed and executed independently: one invalid id is reported as invalid_approval for that id only and does not reject the whole request, so a valid approval in the same batch is never left claimed but unexecuted. TESTS MUST ASSERT (checked in review): PGlite with 042: claim twice -> claimed then not_pending; claim with another orgId -> not_found; claim with wrong conversationId -> not_found; recordPendingApproval twice with the same toolCallId returns the same id and leaves one row; attachApprovalIds does not overwrite an existing approval_id; extractApprovalRequests ignores parts in other states; a fake-client test asserts every .from('copilot_approvals') chain in the module calls .eq('organization_id', ...)

tasks.title: Chat route rewrite: strict body, server history, early approvals, registry tools, 8 steps, memory, 120 s with internal deadline
